title: Linear algebra
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn linear algebra for computing: vectors and dot products, linear systems and Gaussian elimination, matrix operations, inverses and LU factorization, vector spaces, bases and rank, linear transformations and graphics, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, Markov chains, orthogonality and least squares, and the singular value decomposition.

blocks.deliverable: Solve systems by elimination, by hand and in code.
Implement matrix multiplication and elimination in Python.
Find bases for the four fundamental subspaces.
Compute the long-run behavior of a Markov chain.
Fit a line by least squares and compress a matrix with the SVD.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Applied linear algebra: implement a small matrix library in plain Python (multiplication, solving systems, determinants, and power iteration for the top eigenvector), then use it to rank pages with PageRank on a supplied link graph and to fit a least-squares model to supplied data.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
